wholeQuestion.question: Hyperkalemia directly stimulates a cortical zone. Which response is best?
choices: Predict increased medullary aldosterone synthesis.
Predict reduced aldosterone synthesis as the normal potassium response.
Localize the principal aldosterone response to the zona reticularis.
Predict increased zona glomerulosa aldosterone synthesis.
wholeQuestion.rationale: Potassium is a major direct regulator of glomerulosa output.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Adrenal Cortex Zones and Hormone Outputs
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: The adrenal cortex is chemically organized by zone, with enzyme expression and regulators directing cholesterol toward mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids, or adrenal androgens.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Locate a pathway or drug effect in the correct cortical zone before predicting changes in blood pressure, metabolism, stress response, or androgen exposure.

lesson.heading: Assign the glomerulosa
lesson.body: The outer zona glomerulosa produces aldosterone. Angiotensin II and potassium are principal regulators, and aldosterone synthase completes the mineralocorticoid pathway. This zone lacks meaningful CYP17A1 activity, which limits cortisol and androgen synthesis.

lesson.heading: Assign the fasciculata
lesson.body: The middle zona fasciculata produces cortisol under strong ACTH regulation. Its enzyme pattern supports 17-hydroxylation and 11-beta-hydroxylation but not the final aldosterone-synthase sequence.

lesson.heading: Assign the reticularis
lesson.body: The inner zona reticularis produces DHEA, DHEA sulfate, androstenedione, and related adrenal androgens. ACTH contributes to regulation, while enzyme balance favors 17,20-lyase activity and androgen precursors.

keyPoints: Glomerulosa makes aldosterone.
Fasciculata makes cortisol.
Reticularis makes adrenal androgens.
Zone-specific enzymes determine which branch can finish.

check.question: Which regulator most directly stimulates aldosterone production in the zona glomerulosa?
choices: Angiotensin II
Thyroid-stimulating hormone
Growth hormone
Prolactin
check.rationale: Angiotensin II and potassium are major direct regulators of zona glomerulosa aldosterone synthesis.

wholeQuestion.question: Fludrocortisone is increased and the patient develops hypertension and hypokalemia. Which response is best?
choices: Interpret the pattern as inadequate sodium-retaining activity requiring an automatic dose increase.
Evaluate excessive mineralocorticoid action.
Exclude fludrocortisone because mineralocorticoids cannot affect potassium.
Explain hypertension and potassium loss as the expected result of mineralocorticoid receptor blockade.
wholeQuestion.rationale: The electrolyte and pressure pattern follows enhanced distal sodium reabsorption and potassium secretion.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Mineralocorticoid Receptor and 11-Beta-HSD2
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Aldosterone achieves tissue selectivity not because cortisol cannot bind the mineralocorticoid receptor, but because selected tissues enzymatically protect that receptor from cortisol.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Predict mineralocorticoid effects from receptor affinity, local prereceptor metabolism, renal delivery, and the intrinsic activity of the steroid used.

lesson.heading: Recognize receptor overlap
lesson.body: The mineralocorticoid receptor, or NR3C2, can bind aldosterone and cortisol with high affinity. Circulating cortisol is far more abundant, so receptor selectivity requires local enzymatic control rather than ligand affinity alone.

lesson.heading: Protect the receptor
lesson.body: In aldosterone-sensitive epithelia, 11-beta-HSD2 converts active cortisol to cortisone, which has little mineralocorticoid receptor activity. Inhibition or deficiency of this enzyme allows cortisol to drive sodium retention, potassium loss, and hypertension.

lesson.heading: Translate signaling into transport
lesson.body: Activated mineralocorticoid receptor increases epithelial sodium transport and supports potassium and hydrogen secretion in the distal nephron. Fludrocortisone exploits this pathway, while glucocorticoids differ markedly in residual mineralocorticoid activity.

lesson.heading: Monitor replacement in its disease context
lesson.body: For primary adrenal insufficiency with confirmed aldosterone deficiency, monitor salt craving, postural symptoms, edema, blood pressure and electrolytes during fludrocortisone replacement. The endocrine guideline advises against routine salt restriction in this setting. Hypertension prompts dose reassessment; persistent hypertension may need antihypertensive treatment while necessary replacement continues. Do not automatically transfer this plan to glucocorticoid-induced insufficiency.

lesson.heading: Recognize potassium-lowering combinations
lesson.body: Fludrocortisone can amplify potassium loss from loop or thiazide diuretics and amphotericin B. Hypokalemia can increase digoxin-related arrhythmia risk. Check electrolytes and the full medication list when weakness, palpitations or excess fluid retention develops; correct the cause rather than assuming replacement doses cannot cause harm.

keyPoints: Cortisol can bind the mineralocorticoid receptor.
11-beta-HSD2 protects aldosterone-sensitive tissues.
MR activation promotes sodium retention and potassium loss.
Steroids differ in mineralocorticoid activity.

check.question: Why does cortisol not normally dominate mineralocorticoid receptors in the distal nephron?
choices: 11-beta-HSD2 converts cortisol to cortisone locally
Cortisol cannot enter renal cells
Aldosterone is always more concentrated than cortisol
CYP11A1 removes the mineralocorticoid receptor
check.rationale: Local cortisol inactivation creates prereceptor selectivity for aldosterone in protected epithelia.

wholeQuestion.question: A patient has severe infection, profound hypokalemia, and rapidly progressive ACTH-dependent disease. Which response is best?
choices: Delay cortisol treatment until the source is perfectly localized.
Treat potassium alone and ignore infection and cortisol toxicity.
Assume rapid progression excludes ectopic secretion.
Begin urgent cortisol control during ectopic-source evaluation.
wholeQuestion.rationale: Severe cortisol toxicity requires parallel treatment and localization.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Localizing the Source
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Imaging localizes a biochemically classified disorder. It does not prove hormone secretion merely because a pituitary or adrenal lesion is visible.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Require biochemical concordance before attributing causality to an image and use expert inferior petrosal sinus sampling when ACTH-dependent disease remains unresolved.

lesson.heading: Image the correct branch
lesson.body: Pituitary MRI follows ACTH-dependent classification, while adrenal CT or MRI follows ACTH-independent classification. Small pituitary lesions and adrenal nodules are common enough that imaging must remain subordinate to endocrine evidence.

lesson.heading: Separate pituitary from ectopic ACTH
lesson.body: When pituitary imaging is negative, equivocal, or discordant, bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling can compare central and peripheral ACTH after appropriate stimulation. Confirm active hypercortisolism before sampling, especially with cyclic disease. The test distinguishes a pituitary source but does not reliably lateralize every microadenoma.

lesson.heading: Search for ectopic disease deliberately
lesson.body: Ectopic ACTH evaluation is guided by biochemical evidence, disease tempo, potassium and androgen patterns, and targeted imaging. Severe rapid hypercortisolism may require cortisol control while localization proceeds.

keyPoints: Biochemistry determines which anatomy to image.
Incidental lesions do not prove causality.
Petrosal sinus sampling distinguishes pituitary from ectopic ACTH in selected cases.
Severe disease may need treatment before localization is complete.

check.question: Why should a small pituitary lesion not automatically be labeled Cushing disease?
choices: Pituitary incidentalomas exist and the lesion must fit biochemical localization
Pituitary tumors never secrete ACTH
MRI directly measures cortisol
Adrenal CT is always diagnostic
check.rationale: An imaging finding is causal only when it matches the endocrine branch and localization evidence.

wholeQuestion.question: Hypertension and hypokalemia worsen as cortisol rises. Which response is best?
choices: Assume high cortisol cannot activate mineralocorticoid receptors.
Treat hypokalemia as proof of cortisol deficiency.
Address cortisol-mediated mineralocorticoid receptor activation.
Ignore cortisol control after one potassium replacement dose.
wholeQuestion.rationale: Excess cortisol can escape prereceptor protection.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Severity, Comorbidity, and Urgent Control
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Cortisol excess increases short-term and long-term risk through infection, thrombosis, hypertension, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, psychiatric disease, myopathy, fracture, and cardiovascular injury.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Treat the patient and the cortisol simultaneously, with urgent specialist management when rapidly progressive disease, severe infection, psychosis, heart failure, uncontrolled diabetes, or profound hypokalemia threatens life.

lesson.heading: Grade the clinical urgency
lesson.body: Severe Cushing syndrome can deteriorate before a definitive operation is available. Infection may present with muted inflammatory signs, thrombosis risk is increased, and profound cortisol excess can activate mineralocorticoid receptors and produce hypertension and hypokalemia.

lesson.heading: Treat cortisol-dependent injury
lesson.body: Control blood pressure, potassium, glucose, infection, thrombosis risk, bone loss, and psychiatric symptoms while reducing cortisol exposure. Management is individualized because comorbidities, drug interactions, and procedural timing alter the safest plan.

lesson.heading: Use rapid control when necessary
lesson.body: Very severe disease may require rapidly titrated oral steroidogenesis inhibition, combination therapy, block-and-replace management, or urgent bilateral adrenalectomy. Intravenous etomidate can suppress cortisol synthesis in a closely monitored inpatient setting, usually intensive care, when immediate control is required and oral treatment is not feasible, with continuous specialist monitoring and glucocorticoid replacement readiness.

keyPoints: Cushing syndrome is a multisystem emergency when severe.
Infection and thrombosis deserve active surveillance.
Intravenous etomidate is an expert critical-care bridge when oral therapy is not feasible.
Comorbidity treatment continues before and after cortisol normalization.

check.question: Which finding most strongly raises urgency in a patient with known Cushing syndrome?
choices: Severe hypokalemia with infection and rapidly worsening hyperglycemia
Stable freckles
Isolated mild fatigue after one poor night of sleep
Normal blood pressure and glucose
check.rationale: Severe metabolic and infectious complications signal dangerous cortisol excess requiring urgent control.

wholeQuestion.question: Cortisol normalizes but hypertension, edema, and hypokalemia emerge during treatment. Which response is best?
choices: Ignore new potassium and blood-pressure abnormalities because cortisol normalized.
Evaluate precursor accumulation and the treatment regimen rather than assuming disease progression alone.
Increase osilodrostat automatically without investigating toxicity.
Treat the pattern as proof that no adrenal precursors remain.
wholeQuestion.rationale: The biochemical branch above CYP11B1 remains active.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Medicinal Chemistry of Cortisol Control
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Cushing medicines exploit two different molecular strategies: coordinate the heme environment of steroidogenic CYP enzymes to slow cortisol synthesis, or occupy the glucocorticoid receptor without activating it.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Read each scaffold as a clue to target and toxicity, then connect enzyme position or receptor selectivity to the laboratory pattern that follows.

lesson.heading: Coordinate steroidogenic CYP enzymes
lesson.body: Ketoconazole and levoketoconazole contain an imidazole nitrogen that can coordinate CYP heme iron. That interaction explains broad steroidogenic CYP inhibition, extensive interaction potential, and the need to separate enzyme blockade from organ toxicity.

lesson.heading: Aim nearer the terminal cortisol step
lesson.body: Metyrapone uses a pyridine-containing scaffold to inhibit CYP11B1, while osilodrostat is a nonsteroidal inhibitor with greater CYP11B1 potency in vitro. Enzyme potency alone does not establish superior clinical safety or outcomes. Blocking 11-beta-hydroxylase lowers cortisol but raises 11-deoxycortisol and can divert precursors toward mineralocorticoid or androgen activity.

lesson.heading: Antagonize the receptor
lesson.body: Mifepristone preserves a steroid-like framework but carries substituents that favor glucocorticoid and progesterone receptor antagonism. Receptor blockade explains why clinical response replaces cortisol concentration as the treatment endpoint and why pregnancy and endometrial safety cannot be separated from its pharmacology.

lesson.heading: Keep chemistry clinically bounded
lesson.body: Aminoglutethimide and trilostane illustrate older approaches to upstream steroid synthesis, but they are not presented as routine contemporary Cushing therapy. Relacorilant is a selective glucocorticoid receptor antagonist, but its current US approval is for an oncology indication, not endogenous Cushing syndrome.

keyPoints: A coordinating nitrogen can support CYP heme binding.
CYP11B1 blockade raises 11-deoxycortisol and upstream precursors.
Mifepristone receptor pharmacology connects cortisol antagonism with antiprogestin effects.
A mechanistically relevant drug is not automatically approved for Cushing syndrome.

check.question: What structural feature helps explain broad steroidogenic CYP inhibition by ketoconazole-derived therapy?
choices: An imidazole nitrogen that can coordinate CYP heme iron
A permanently charged quaternary ammonium group
A beta-lactam ring
A phosphate polymer that traps cortisol
check.rationale: The imidazole nitrogen can coordinate the heme iron within CYP enzymes and helps explain both steroidogenic inhibition and interaction burden.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Adrenal Steroidogenesis Inhibitors
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Steroidogenesis inhibitors lower cortisol by blocking adrenal enzymes, but each target creates a distinct pattern of speed, precursor accumulation, interaction, and organ toxicity.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Select and titrate from severity, speed, liver and cardiac risk, pregnancy potential, interactions, access, and the need for biochemical monitoring rather than treating the class as interchangeable.

lesson.heading: Block CYP11B1
lesson.body: Osilodrostat and metyrapone inhibit 11-beta-hydroxylase, lowering cortisol while increasing upstream precursors. Monitor for hypocortisolism, hypokalemia, hypertension, edema, androgenic effects, and QT-related risk where applicable.

lesson.heading: Apply the osilodrostat label
lesson.body: Isturisa now covers adult endogenous Cushing syndrome when surgery is unavailable or unsuccessful. Usual initiation is 2 mg twice daily; increases are spaced at least two weeks apart, with a 30 mg twice-daily ceiling. Hepatic impairment requires lower starting doses. Correct potassium and magnesium, obtain an ECG before treatment and within one week, and follow cortisol and symptoms during titration. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors require halving the dose. Cortisol suppression can persist after stopping treatment; symptomatic adrenal insufficiency requires drug interruption and glucocorticoid treatment.

lesson.heading: Use azole chemistry carefully
lesson.body: Levoketoconazole inhibits several steroidogenic CYP enzymes and carries important hepatic injury and QT prolongation risks plus substantial interaction potential. Historical oral ketoconazole use requires the same recognition that fungal and adrenal CYP inhibition are not selective.

lesson.heading: Make levoketoconazole monitoring explicit
lesson.body: Recorlev starts at 150 mg twice daily; increase the total daily dose by 150 mg no sooner than every two to three weeks, up to 600 mg twice daily. Check liver enzymes and bilirubin weekly for six weeks, every two weeks for six more weeks, then monthly for three months. Obtain an ECG before each increase. Baseline QTcF above 470 ms, specified liver disorders, and certain interacting drugs are contraindications, not merely reasons for closer observation. Consult the label for interruption and permanent-discontinuation thresholds. Recorlev is not approved as an antifungal.

lesson.heading: Choose titration strategy
lesson.body: A titration-to-normal approach adjusts drug to biochemical and clinical response. In severe or highly variable disease, expert teams may fully block cortisol synthesis and add physiologic glucocorticoid replacement. Every approach requires education for hypocortisolism and stress illness.

keyPoints: CYP11B1 blockade raises upstream precursors.
Levoketoconazole requires liver, ECG, and interaction review.
Hypocortisolism can occur with every effective synthesis inhibitor.
Block and replace belongs in experienced multidisciplinary care.

choices: 11-beta-hydroxylase, CYP11B1

Dipeptidyl peptidase 4
HMG-CoA reductase
check.rationale: Both drugs lower cortisol chiefly by inhibiting the terminal CYP11B1 step.

wholeQuestion.question: A patient has new hypertension, edema, and hypokalemia after heavy licorice tea use. Which response is best?
choices: Stop glycyrrhizin exposure and evaluate the electrolyte and cardiovascular consequences.
Treat licorice tea as irrelevant to electrolyte findings
Recommend additional licorice for the edema
Assume hypokalemia rules out a mineralocorticoid-like effect
wholeQuestion.explanation: The clinical pattern is consistent with licorice-induced pseudoaldosteronism.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Recognize High-Consequence Organ Toxicity
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Supplement injury can present as liver failure, arrhythmia, hypertension, hypokalemia, seizure, or kidney injury. Product variability and multi-ingredient blends make causal assessment difficult but do not justify delayed care.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Stop the suspected exposure when serious toxicity is possible, stabilize the patient, preserve product details, and evaluate competing causes.

lesson.heading: Protect the liver
lesson.body: Kava has been linked to rare, sometimes severe liver injury. Concentrated green tea extracts have also been associated with rare injury and should not be equated with ordinary brewed tea. Black cohosh reports require safety action while causal certainty is assessed.

lesson.heading: Recognize prohibited and unsafe stimulants
lesson.body: Dietary supplements containing ephedrine alkaloids are banned. FDA considers DMAA-containing products illegal and unsafe. Bitter orange products can contain synephrine, while yohimbe products can produce serious cardiovascular and neurologic effects. Online availability does not establish legality or safety.

lesson.heading: Identify concentrated 7-OH products
lesson.body: FDA advises consumers to avoid products with added or enhanced 7-hydroxymitragynine, also called 7-OH. These tablets, gummies, shots, drink mixes, and similar products are potent opioid exposures. They are not lawful dietary supplements, cannot lawfully be added to conventional foods, and are not FDA-approved drugs. Trace 7-OH in the kratom plant should not be treated as equivalent to a concentrated product. Reported harms include addiction, withdrawal, anxiety, depression, gastrointestinal distress, insomnia, and seizures.

lesson.heading: Identify licorice physiology
lesson.body: Glycyrrhizin-containing licorice can inhibit cortisol metabolism at the mineralocorticoid receptor environment, producing sodium retention, hypertension, edema, hypokalemia, and arrhythmia. Licorice flavoring may not contain the same exposure, so the exact product matters.

lesson.heading: Prevent avoidable product harms
lesson.body: Vinpocetine should be avoided during pregnancy and when pregnancy is possible because of FDA fetal-harm concerns. Butterbur can contain liver-toxic pyrrolizidine alkaloids; even products described as PA-free have rare liver-injury reports. A historical migraine recommendation is not a current safety endorsement.

lesson.heading: Treat the product as evidence
lesson.body: Save the bottle or label, capture lot and source, and look for duplicate stimulants, adulterants, and recent reformulation. Serious events warrant current FDA reporting even when causality is not fully proven.

keyPoints: Kava and concentrated green tea extract can threaten the liver.
Concentrated 7-OH products are potent opioid exposures, not lawful supplements.
Licorice can cause hypokalemic hypertension.
Serious events require care before causal certainty.

check.question: A patient develops withdrawal symptoms and seizures after using concentrated 7-OH gummies sold as supplements. What is the best interpretation?
choices: Treat this as a potentially serious opioid exposure and seek urgent clinical and poison-center guidance
Assume the product is safe because 7-OH occurs in trace plant amounts
Treat it as an FDA-approved withdrawal medicine
Use more product to suppress every symptom
check.rationale: FDA identifies concentrated 7-OH products as potent opioid exposures associated with serious harm and advises consumers to avoid them.

wholeQuestion.question: A patient on voclosporin develops hypertension, hyperkalemia, tremor, and falling eGFR. What is the best response?
choices: Reassess exposure and apply current dose-hold or discontinuation guidance urgently.
Continue full dosing without reviewing the renal decline.
Increase the dose because tremor proves inadequate exposure.
Treat potassium elevation as reassuring evidence of efficacy.
wholeQuestion.explanation: The toxicity pattern is consistent with calcineurin inhibition and requires structured renal and cardiovascular response.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Detect and Treat Lupus Nephritis Early
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Kidney injury can be clinically quiet until proteinuria, active sediment, hypertension, or declining function becomes visible. Contemporary care screens earlier, biopsies at a lower threshold, and often combines therapies from the start.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Treat the biopsy, renal trajectory, and whole patient, then make proteinuria and kidney function the authoritative response record.

lesson.heading: Screen before symptoms
lesson.body: In SLE without known kidney disease, quantify urine protein at least every six to twelve months and during extra-renal flares. New urine abnormalities, hypertension, edema, or kidney dysfunction require faster evaluation.

lesson.heading: Use biopsy to direct treatment
lesson.body: Current ACR guidance conditionally recommends biopsy when urine protein exceeds 0.5 g/g and or kidney function is impaired without another explanation. Histology separates active, chronic, proliferative, and membranous patterns that require different strategies. Suspected active nephritis warrants prompt specialist-directed glucocorticoids while awaiting biopsy and histopathology; do not delay urgent inflammatory treatment solely for the report.

lesson.heading: Build contemporary combination therapy
lesson.body: For active class III or IV nephritis, current options pair glucocorticoid with mycophenolate plus belimumab, mycophenolate plus a calcineurin inhibitor, or low-dose cyclophosphamide plus belimumab. Pure class V disease with proteinuria at least 1 g/g favors glucocorticoid, mycophenolate, and calcineurin inhibition.

lesson.heading: Choose the regimen and steroid course deliberately
lesson.body: ACR conditionally favors mycophenolic acid analog regimens over cyclophosphamide regimens. In class III/IV disease, proteinuria at least 3 g/g favors a mycophenolate-plus-CNI combination; moderate to severe active extrarenal manifestations favor a belimumab-containing combination. Low eGFR, uncontrolled blood pressure, or substantial chronic biopsy damage can instead favor belimumab over a CNI because of nephrotoxicity and hypertension risk. The Euro-Lupus low-dose cyclophosphamide course is 500 mg IV every two weeks for six doses, followed by substitution with a mycophenolic acid analog. For active class III/IV disease, the ACR MMF target is 2 to 3 g/day, adjusted for tolerability and clinical context; it is not a tablet-for-tablet substitution with enteric-coated mycophenolic acid. The adult glucocorticoid framework is IV methylprednisolone 250 to 1,000 mg daily for one to three days, then oral prednisone-equivalent at most 0.5 mg/kg/day, capped at 40 mg/day, tapered to at most 5 mg/day by six months. Pediatric dosing requires adjustment rather than automatic use of adult pulse doses.

lesson.heading: Define renal response numerically
lesson.body: ACR defines complete response as proteinuria below 0.5 g/g with kidney function stable or improved and at least 80% of baseline. Partial response requires at least a 50% proteinuria reduction to below 3 g/g, also with kidney function at least 80% of baseline. Assess these targets over six to twelve months; complete response may take longer. For example, 4.0 to 1.8 g/g is a 55% fall: with stable kidney function it meets partial, not complete, response. These consensus definitions do not substitute for the full trajectory or imply histologic remission.

lesson.heading: Distinguish response from deterioration
lesson.body: Do not wait six months when kidney function is falling rapidly or proteinuria is rising: reassess and change therapy earlier, even within three months. A patient improving on triple therapy with partial response may continue that regimen under close review; partial response after dual therapy conditionally favors escalation to triple therapy. Failure of two appropriate treatment courses warrants specialist reassessment for refractory disease, including activity versus irreversible damage.

lesson.heading: Recognize other biopsy patterns
lesson.body: Pure class V disease below 1 g/g proteinuria is not automatically untreated: ACR conditionally favors glucocorticoid and/or MPAA, azathioprine, or a CNI, with very limited evidence. Class II disease, podocytopathy, and thrombotic microangiopathy need their own nephrology assessment. A thrombotic biopsy pattern can reflect APS, TTP, complement-mediated disease, or another cause; do not apply the proliferative-nephritis regimen indiscriminately.

lesson.heading: Interpret incomplete response
lesson.body: First verify dose, actual exposure, access, and competing kidney diagnoses. If at least a partial response has not occurred by six to twelve months, ACR conditionally favors escalation: dual therapy to triple therapy, or initial triple therapy to an alternative combination or selected anti-CD20 treatment. Repeat biopsy can be appropriate for suspected relapse or ongoing renal abnormalities after at least six months of adequate treatment. After complete response, the guideline recommends at least three to five years of total immunosuppressive treatment; this is not permission to stop when proteinuria first improves.

lesson.heading: Continue the regimen that achieved response
lesson.body: After complete response to triple therapy, ACR conditionally favors continuing that immunosuppressive regimen. After complete response to dual glucocorticoid plus cyclophosphamide or MPAA therapy, ongoing MPAA is conditionally preferred over azathioprine. Pregnancy plans, intolerance, access, and individual risk can change this choice; complete response is not an instruction to withdraw all treatment.

lesson.heading: Preserve kidney health beyond immune control
lesson.body: With elevated proteinuria, consider renin-angiotensin system inhibition when appropriate, while accounting for potassium, kidney function, and pregnancy. Nephrotic thrombotic risk may warrant a nephrology discussion about anticoagulation. For end-stage kidney disease, ACR favors transplantation over long-term dialysis when suitable; ongoing rheumatology follow-up remains necessary after dialysis or transplantation. Transplant timing does not require complete serologic remission if no other major organ involvement is present.

lesson.heading: Adapt follow-up across life stages
lesson.body: In children, monitor growth and pubertal development and arrange a structured transition to adult care. In older adults, regularly reassess polypharmacy and doses as kidney function changes. Nephrology should consider preemptive transplantation when progressive kidney failure approaches an eGFR of 15, rather than assuming dialysis must come first.

lesson.heading: Monitor response and toxicity
lesson.body: Quantify proteinuria at least every three months until complete response, then every three to six months during sustained response. Unexpected spot protein-to-creatinine results should be confirmed with a 24-hour collection, especially before changing therapy. Track kidney function, urine sediment, blood pressure, adherence, infection, marrow, and product-specific toxicity. Complement and anti-dsDNA are checked at clinic visits, no more often than monthly under the ACR good-practice statement; they supplement rather than replace renal outcomes. Voclosporin requires close eGFR, potassium, pressure, neurologic, QT, and interaction review.

keyPoints: Screen urine even when SLE seems quiet.
Biopsy is a treatment tool.
Modern nephritis care often begins with combination therapy.
Proteinuria and kidney function anchor response.

wholeQuestion.question: Hyperkalemia directly stimulates a cortical zone. Which response is best?
choices: Predict increased medullary aldosterone synthesis.
Predict reduced aldosterone synthesis as the normal potassium response.
Localize the principal aldosterone response to the zona reticularis.
Predict increased zona glomerulosa aldosterone synthesis.
wholeQuestion.rationale: Potassium is a major direct regulator of glomerulosa output.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Adrenal Cortex Zones and Hormone Outputs
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: The adrenal cortex is chemically organized by zone, with enzyme expression and regulators directing cholesterol toward mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids, or adrenal androgens.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Locate a pathway or drug effect in the correct cortical zone before predicting changes in blood pressure, metabolism, stress response, or androgen exposure.

lesson.heading: Assign the glomerulosa
lesson.body: The outer zona glomerulosa produces aldosterone. Angiotensin II and potassium are principal regulators, and aldosterone synthase completes the mineralocorticoid pathway. This zone lacks meaningful CYP17A1 activity, which limits cortisol and androgen synthesis.

lesson.heading: Assign the fasciculata
lesson.body: The middle zona fasciculata produces cortisol under strong ACTH regulation. Its enzyme pattern supports 17-hydroxylation and 11-beta-hydroxylation but not the final aldosterone-synthase sequence.

lesson.heading: Assign the reticularis
lesson.body: The inner zona reticularis produces DHEA, DHEA sulfate, androstenedione, and related adrenal androgens. ACTH contributes to regulation, while enzyme balance favors 17,20-lyase activity and androgen precursors.

keyPoints: Glomerulosa makes aldosterone.
Fasciculata makes cortisol.
Reticularis makes adrenal androgens.
Zone-specific enzymes determine which branch can finish.

check.rationale: Angiotensin II and potassium are major direct regulators of zona glomerulosa aldosterone synthesis.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Mineralocorticoid Receptor and 11-Beta-HSD2
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Aldosterone achieves tissue selectivity not because cortisol cannot bind the mineralocorticoid receptor, but because selected tissues enzymatically protect that receptor from cortisol.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Predict mineralocorticoid effects from receptor affinity, local prereceptor metabolism, renal delivery, and the intrinsic activity of the steroid used.

lesson.heading: Recognize receptor overlap
lesson.body: The mineralocorticoid receptor, or NR3C2, can bind aldosterone and cortisol with high affinity. Circulating cortisol is far more abundant, so receptor selectivity requires local enzymatic control rather than ligand affinity alone.

lesson.heading: Protect the receptor
lesson.body: In aldosterone-sensitive epithelia, 11-beta-HSD2 converts active cortisol to cortisone, which has little mineralocorticoid receptor activity. Inhibition or deficiency of this enzyme allows cortisol to drive sodium retention, potassium loss, and hypertension.

lesson.heading: Translate signaling into transport
lesson.body: Activated mineralocorticoid receptor increases epithelial sodium transport and supports potassium and hydrogen secretion in the distal nephron. Fludrocortisone exploits this pathway, while glucocorticoids differ markedly in residual mineralocorticoid activity.

lesson.heading: Monitor replacement in its disease context
lesson.body: For primary adrenal insufficiency with confirmed aldosterone deficiency, monitor salt craving, postural symptoms, edema, blood pressure and electrolytes during fludrocortisone replacement. The endocrine guideline advises against routine salt restriction in this setting. Hypertension prompts dose reassessment; persistent hypertension may need antihypertensive treatment while necessary replacement continues. Do not automatically transfer this plan to glucocorticoid-induced insufficiency.

lesson.heading: Recognize potassium-lowering combinations
lesson.body: Fludrocortisone can amplify potassium loss from loop or thiazide diuretics and amphotericin B. Hypokalemia can increase digoxin-related arrhythmia risk. Check electrolytes and the full medication list when weakness, palpitations or excess fluid retention develops; correct the cause rather than assuming replacement doses cannot cause harm.

keyPoints: Cortisol can bind the mineralocorticoid receptor.
11-beta-HSD2 protects aldosterone-sensitive tissues.
MR activation promotes sodium retention and potassium loss.
Steroids differ in mineralocorticoid activity.

check.question: Why does cortisol not normally dominate mineralocorticoid receptors in the distal nephron?
choices: 11-beta-HSD2 converts cortisol to cortisone locally
Cortisol cannot enter renal cells
Aldosterone is always more concentrated than cortisol
CYP11A1 removes the mineralocorticoid receptor
check.rationale: Local cortisol inactivation creates prereceptor selectivity for aldosterone in protected epithelia.

wholeQuestion.question: A patient has severe infection, profound hypokalemia, and rapidly progressive ACTH-dependent disease. Which response is best?
choices: Delay cortisol treatment until the source is perfectly localized.
Treat potassium alone and ignore infection and cortisol toxicity.
Assume rapid progression excludes ectopic secretion.
Begin urgent cortisol control during ectopic-source evaluation.
wholeQuestion.rationale: Severe cortisol toxicity requires parallel treatment and localization.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Localizing the Source
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Imaging localizes a biochemically classified disorder. It does not prove hormone secretion merely because a pituitary or adrenal lesion is visible.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Require biochemical concordance before attributing causality to an image and use expert inferior petrosal sinus sampling when ACTH-dependent disease remains unresolved.

lesson.heading: Image the correct branch
lesson.body: Pituitary MRI follows ACTH-dependent classification, while adrenal CT or MRI follows ACTH-independent classification. Small pituitary lesions and adrenal nodules are common enough that imaging must remain subordinate to endocrine evidence.

lesson.heading: Separate pituitary from ectopic ACTH
lesson.body: When pituitary imaging is negative, equivocal, or discordant, bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling can compare central and peripheral ACTH after appropriate stimulation. Confirm active hypercortisolism before sampling, especially with cyclic disease. The test distinguishes a pituitary source but does not reliably lateralize every microadenoma.

lesson.heading: Search for ectopic disease deliberately
lesson.body: Ectopic ACTH evaluation is guided by biochemical evidence, disease tempo, potassium and androgen patterns, and targeted imaging. Severe rapid hypercortisolism may require cortisol control while localization proceeds.

keyPoints: Biochemistry determines which anatomy to image.
Incidental lesions do not prove causality.
Petrosal sinus sampling distinguishes pituitary from ectopic ACTH in selected cases.
Severe disease may need treatment before localization is complete.

check.question: Why should a small pituitary lesion not automatically be labeled Cushing disease?
choices: Pituitary incidentalomas exist and the lesion must fit biochemical localization
Pituitary tumors never secrete ACTH
MRI directly measures cortisol
Adrenal CT is always diagnostic
check.rationale: An imaging finding is causal only when it matches the endocrine branch and localization evidence.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Severity, Comorbidity, and Urgent Control
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Cortisol excess increases short-term and long-term risk through infection, thrombosis, hypertension, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, psychiatric disease, myopathy, fracture, and cardiovascular injury.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Treat the patient and the cortisol simultaneously, with urgent specialist management when rapidly progressive disease, severe infection, psychosis, heart failure, uncontrolled diabetes, or profound hypokalemia threatens life.

lesson.heading: Grade the clinical urgency
lesson.body: Severe Cushing syndrome can deteriorate before a definitive operation is available. Infection may present with muted inflammatory signs, thrombosis risk is increased, and profound cortisol excess can activate mineralocorticoid receptors and produce hypertension and hypokalemia.

lesson.heading: Treat cortisol-dependent injury
lesson.body: Control blood pressure, potassium, glucose, infection, thrombosis risk, bone loss, and psychiatric symptoms while reducing cortisol exposure. Management is individualized because comorbidities, drug interactions, and procedural timing alter the safest plan.

lesson.heading: Use rapid control when necessary
lesson.body: Very severe disease may require rapidly titrated oral steroidogenesis inhibition, combination therapy, block-and-replace management, or urgent bilateral adrenalectomy. Intravenous etomidate can suppress cortisol synthesis in a closely monitored inpatient setting, usually intensive care, when immediate control is required and oral treatment is not feasible, with continuous specialist monitoring and glucocorticoid replacement readiness.

keyPoints: Cushing syndrome is a multisystem emergency when severe.
Infection and thrombosis deserve active surveillance.
Intravenous etomidate is an expert critical-care bridge when oral therapy is not feasible.
Comorbidity treatment continues before and after cortisol normalization.

Increase osilodrostat automatically without investigating toxicity.
Treat the pattern as proof that no adrenal precursors remain.
wholeQuestion.rationale: The biochemical branch above CYP11B1 remains active.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Medicinal Chemistry of Cortisol Control
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Cushing medicines exploit two different molecular strategies: coordinate the heme environment of steroidogenic CYP enzymes to slow cortisol synthesis, or occupy the glucocorticoid receptor without activating it.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Read each scaffold as a clue to target and toxicity, then connect enzyme position or receptor selectivity to the laboratory pattern that follows.

lesson.heading: Coordinate steroidogenic CYP enzymes
lesson.body: Ketoconazole and levoketoconazole contain an imidazole nitrogen that can coordinate CYP heme iron. That interaction explains broad steroidogenic CYP inhibition, extensive interaction potential, and the need to separate enzyme blockade from organ toxicity.

lesson.heading: Aim nearer the terminal cortisol step
lesson.body: Metyrapone uses a pyridine-containing scaffold to inhibit CYP11B1, while osilodrostat is a nonsteroidal inhibitor with greater CYP11B1 potency in vitro. Enzyme potency alone does not establish superior clinical safety or outcomes. Blocking 11-beta-hydroxylase lowers cortisol but raises 11-deoxycortisol and can divert precursors toward mineralocorticoid or androgen activity.

lesson.heading: Antagonize the receptor
lesson.body: Mifepristone preserves a steroid-like framework but carries substituents that favor glucocorticoid and progesterone receptor antagonism. Receptor blockade explains why clinical response replaces cortisol concentration as the treatment endpoint and why pregnancy and endometrial safety cannot be separated from its pharmacology.

lesson.heading: Keep chemistry clinically bounded
lesson.body: Aminoglutethimide and trilostane illustrate older approaches to upstream steroid synthesis, but they are not presented as routine contemporary Cushing therapy. Relacorilant is a selective glucocorticoid receptor antagonist, but its current US approval is for an oncology indication, not endogenous Cushing syndrome.

keyPoints: A coordinating nitrogen can support CYP heme binding.
CYP11B1 blockade raises 11-deoxycortisol and upstream precursors.
Mifepristone receptor pharmacology connects cortisol antagonism with antiprogestin effects.
A mechanistically relevant drug is not automatically approved for Cushing syndrome.

check.rationale: The imidazole nitrogen can coordinate the heme iron within CYP enzymes and helps explain both steroidogenic inhibition and interaction burden.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Adrenal Steroidogenesis Inhibitors
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Steroidogenesis inhibitors lower cortisol by blocking adrenal enzymes, but each target creates a distinct pattern of speed, precursor accumulation, interaction, and organ toxicity.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Select and titrate from severity, speed, liver and cardiac risk, pregnancy potential, interactions, access, and the need for biochemical monitoring rather than treating the class as interchangeable.

lesson.heading: Block CYP11B1
lesson.body: Osilodrostat and metyrapone inhibit 11-beta-hydroxylase, lowering cortisol while increasing upstream precursors. Monitor for hypocortisolism, hypokalemia, hypertension, edema, androgenic effects, and QT-related risk where applicable.

lesson.heading: Apply the osilodrostat label
lesson.body: Isturisa now covers adult endogenous Cushing syndrome when surgery is unavailable or unsuccessful. Usual initiation is 2 mg twice daily; increases are spaced at least two weeks apart, with a 30 mg twice-daily ceiling. Hepatic impairment requires lower starting doses. Correct potassium and magnesium, obtain an ECG before treatment and within one week, and follow cortisol and symptoms during titration. Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors require halving the dose. Cortisol suppression can persist after stopping treatment; symptomatic adrenal insufficiency requires drug interruption and glucocorticoid treatment.

lesson.heading: Use azole chemistry carefully
lesson.body: Levoketoconazole inhibits several steroidogenic CYP enzymes and carries important hepatic injury and QT prolongation risks plus substantial interaction potential. Historical oral ketoconazole use requires the same recognition that fungal and adrenal CYP inhibition are not selective.

lesson.heading: Make levoketoconazole monitoring explicit
lesson.body: Recorlev starts at 150 mg twice daily; increase the total daily dose by 150 mg no sooner than every two to three weeks, up to 600 mg twice daily. Check liver enzymes and bilirubin weekly for six weeks, every two weeks for six more weeks, then monthly for three months. Obtain an ECG before each increase. Baseline QTcF above 470 ms, specified liver disorders, and certain interacting drugs are contraindications, not merely reasons for closer observation. Consult the label for interruption and permanent-discontinuation thresholds. Recorlev is not approved as an antifungal.

lesson.heading: Choose titration strategy
lesson.body: A titration-to-normal approach adjusts drug to biochemical and clinical response. In severe or highly variable disease, expert teams may fully block cortisol synthesis and add physiologic glucocorticoid replacement. Every approach requires education for hypocortisolism and stress illness.

keyPoints: CYP11B1 blockade raises upstream precursors.
Levoketoconazole requires liver, ECG, and interaction review.
Hypocortisolism can occur with every effective synthesis inhibitor.
Block and replace belongs in experienced multidisciplinary care.

choices: Stop glycyrrhizin exposure and evaluate the electrolyte and cardiovascular consequences.
Treat licorice tea as irrelevant to electrolyte findings
Recommend additional licorice for the edema
Assume hypokalemia rules out a mineralocorticoid-like effect
wholeQuestion.explanation: The clinical pattern is consistent with licorice-induced pseudoaldosteronism.

wholeAssociatedLesson.title: Recognize High-Consequence Organ Toxicity
wholeAssociatedLesson.summary: Supplement injury can present as liver failure, arrhythmia, hypertension, hypokalemia, seizure, or kidney injury. Product variability and multi-ingredient blends make causal assessment difficult but do not justify delayed care.
wholeAssociatedLesson.application: Stop the suspected exposure when serious toxicity is possible, stabilize the patient, preserve product details, and evaluate competing causes.

lesson.heading: Protect the liver
lesson.body: Kava has been linked to rare, sometimes severe liver injury. Concentrated green tea extracts have also been associated with rare injury and should not be equated with ordinary brewed tea. Black cohosh reports require safety action while causal certainty is assessed.

lesson.heading: Recognize prohibited and unsafe stimulants
lesson.body: Dietary supplements containing ephedrine alkaloids are banned. FDA considers DMAA-containing products illegal and unsafe. Bitter orange products can contain synephrine, while yohimbe products can produce serious cardiovascular and neurologic effects. Online availability does not establish legality or safety.

lesson.heading: Identify concentrated 7-OH products
lesson.body: FDA advises consumers to avoid products with added or enhanced 7-hydroxymitragynine, also called 7-OH. These tablets, gummies, shots, drink mixes, and similar products are potent opioid exposures. They are not lawful dietary supplements, cannot lawfully be added to conventional foods, and are not FDA-approved drugs. Trace 7-OH in the kratom plant should not be treated as equivalent to a concentrated product. Reported harms include addiction, withdrawal, anxiety, depression, gastrointestinal distress, insomnia, and seizures.

lesson.heading: Identify licorice physiology
lesson.body: Glycyrrhizin-containing licorice can inhibit cortisol metabolism at the mineralocorticoid receptor environment, producing sodium retention, hypertension, edema, hypokalemia, and arrhythmia. Licorice flavoring may not contain the same exposure, so the exact product matters.

object.title: Adrenal Cortex Zones and Hormone Outputs
object.summary: The adrenal cortex is chemically organized by zone, with enzyme expression and regulators directing cholesterol toward mineralocorticoids, glucocorticoids, or adrenal androgens.
object.application: Locate a pathway or drug effect in the correct cortical zone before predicting changes in blood pressure, metabolism, stress response, or androgen exposure.

lesson.heading: Assign the glomerulosa
lesson.body: The outer zona glomerulosa produces aldosterone. Angiotensin II and potassium are principal regulators, and aldosterone synthase completes the mineralocorticoid pathway. This zone lacks meaningful CYP17A1 activity, which limits cortisol and androgen synthesis.

lesson.heading: Assign the fasciculata
lesson.body: The middle zona fasciculata produces cortisol under strong ACTH regulation. Its enzyme pattern supports 17-hydroxylation and 11-beta-hydroxylation but not the final aldosterone-synthase sequence.

lesson.heading: Assign the reticularis
lesson.body: The inner zona reticularis produces DHEA, DHEA sulfate, androstenedione, and related adrenal androgens. ACTH contributes to regulation, while enzyme balance favors 17,20-lyase activity and androgen precursors.

keyPoints: Glomerulosa makes aldosterone.
Fasciculata makes cortisol.
Reticularis makes adrenal androgens.
Zone-specific enzymes determine which branch can finish.

check.rationale: Angiotensin II and potassium are major direct regulators of zona glomerulosa aldosterone synthesis.

object.title: Mineralocorticoid Receptor and 11-Beta-HSD2
object.summary: Aldosterone achieves tissue selectivity not because cortisol cannot bind the mineralocorticoid receptor, but because selected tissues enzymatically protect that receptor from cortisol.
object.application: Predict mineralocorticoid effects from receptor affinity, local prereceptor metabolism, renal delivery, and the intrinsic activity of the steroid used.

lesson.heading: Recognize receptor overlap
lesson.body: The mineralocorticoid receptor, or NR3C2, can bind aldosterone and cortisol with high affinity. Circulating cortisol is far more abundant, so receptor selectivity requires local enzymatic control rather than ligand affinity alone.

lesson.heading: Protect the receptor
lesson.body: In aldosterone-sensitive epithelia, 11-beta-HSD2 converts active cortisol to cortisone, which has little mineralocorticoid receptor activity. Inhibition or deficiency of this enzyme allows cortisol to drive sodium retention, potassium loss, and hypertension.

lesson.heading: Translate signaling into transport
lesson.body: Activated mineralocorticoid receptor increases epithelial sodium transport and supports potassium and hydrogen secretion in the distal nephron. Fludrocortisone exploits this pathway, while glucocorticoids differ markedly in residual mineralocorticoid activity.

lesson.heading: Monitor replacement in its disease context
lesson.body: For primary adrenal insufficiency with confirmed aldosterone deficiency, monitor salt craving, postural symptoms, edema, blood pressure and electrolytes during fludrocortisone replacement. The endocrine guideline advises against routine salt restriction in this setting. Hypertension prompts dose reassessment; persistent hypertension may need antihypertensive treatment while necessary replacement continues. Do not automatically transfer this plan to glucocorticoid-induced insufficiency.

lesson.heading: Recognize potassium-lowering combinations
lesson.body: Fludrocortisone can amplify potassium loss from loop or thiazide diuretics and amphotericin B. Hypokalemia can increase digoxin-related arrhythmia risk. Check electrolytes and the full medication list when weakness, palpitations or excess fluid retention develops; correct the cause rather than assuming replacement doses cannot cause harm.

keyPoints: Cortisol can bind the mineralocorticoid receptor.
11-beta-HSD2 protects aldosterone-sensitive tissues.
MR activation promotes sodium retention and potassium loss.
Steroids differ in mineralocorticoid activity.

check.rationale: Local cortisol inactivation creates prereceptor selectivity for aldosterone in protected epithelia.

object.title: Localizing the Source
object.summary: Imaging localizes a biochemically classified disorder. It does not prove hormone secretion merely because a pituitary or adrenal lesion is visible.
object.application: Require biochemical concordance before attributing causality to an image and use expert inferior petrosal sinus sampling when ACTH-dependent disease remains unresolved.

lesson.heading: Image the correct branch
lesson.body: Pituitary MRI follows ACTH-dependent classification, while adrenal CT or MRI follows ACTH-independent classification. Small pituitary lesions and adrenal nodules are common enough that imaging must remain subordinate to endocrine evidence.

lesson.heading: Separate pituitary from ectopic ACTH
lesson.body: When pituitary imaging is negative, equivocal, or discordant, bilateral inferior petrosal sinus sampling can compare central and peripheral ACTH after appropriate stimulation. keyPoints: Biochemistry determines which anatomy to image.
Incidental lesions do not prove causality.
Petrosal sinus sampling distinguishes pituitary from ectopic ACTH in selected cases.
Severe disease may need treatment before localization is complete.

Pituitary tumors never secrete ACTH

check.rationale: An imaging finding is causal only when it matches the endocrine branch and localization evidence.

object.title: Severity, Comorbidity, and Urgent Control
object.summary: Cortisol excess increases short-term and long-term risk through infection, thrombosis, hypertension, hypokalemia, hyperglycemia, psychiatric disease, myopathy, fracture, and cardiovascular injury.
object.application: Treat the patient and the cortisol simultaneously, with urgent specialist management when rapidly progressive disease, severe infection, psychosis, heart failure, uncontrolled diabetes, or profound hypokalemia threatens life.

lesson.heading: Grade the clinical urgency
lesson.body: Severe Cushing syndrome can deteriorate before a definitive operation is available. Infection may present with muted inflammatory signs, thrombosis risk is increased, and profound cortisol excess can activate mineralocorticoid receptors and produce hypertension and hypokalemia.

lesson.heading: Treat cortisol-dependent injury
lesson.body: Control blood pressure, potassium, glucose, infection, thrombosis risk, bone loss, and psychiatric symptoms while reducing cortisol exposure. Management is individualized because comorbidities, drug interactions, and procedural timing alter the safest plan.

lesson.heading: Use rapid control when necessary
lesson.body: Very severe disease may require rapidly titrated oral steroidogenesis inhibition, combination therapy, block-and-replace management, or urgent bilateral adrenalectomy. Infection and thrombosis deserve active surveillance.

Comorbidity treatment continues before and after cortisol normalization.

check.question: Which finding most strongly raises urgency in a patient with known Cushing syndrome?

check.rationale: Severe metabolic and infectious complications signal dangerous cortisol excess requiring urgent control.

object.title: Medicinal Chemistry of Cortisol Control
object.summary: Cushing medicines exploit two different molecular strategies: coordinate the heme environment of steroidogenic CYP enzymes to slow cortisol synthesis, or occupy the glucocorticoid receptor without activating it.
object.application: Read each scaffold as a clue to target and toxicity, then connect enzyme position or receptor selectivity to the laboratory pattern that follows.

lesson.heading: Coordinate steroidogenic CYP enzymes
lesson.body: Ketoconazole and levoketoconazole contain an imidazole nitrogen that can coordinate CYP heme iron. That interaction explains broad steroidogenic CYP inhibition, extensive interaction potential, and the need to separate enzyme blockade from organ toxicity.

lesson.body: Metyrapone uses a pyridine-containing scaffold to inhibit CYP11B1, while osilodrostat is a nonsteroidal inhibitor with greater CYP11B1 potency in vitro. Enzyme potency alone does not establish superior clinical safety or outcomes. Blocking 11-beta-hydroxylase lowers cortisol but raises 11-deoxycortisol and can divert precursors toward mineralocorticoid or androgen activity.

lesson.heading: Antagonize the receptor
lesson.body: Mifepristone preserves a steroid-like framework but carries substituents that favor glucocorticoid and progesterone receptor antagonism. Receptor blockade explains why clinical response replaces cortisol concentration as the treatment endpoint and why pregnancy and endometrial safety cannot be separated from its pharmacology.

lesson.heading: Keep chemistry clinically bounded
lesson.body: Aminoglutethimide and trilostane illustrate older approaches to upstream steroid synthesis, but they are not presented as routine contemporary Cushing therapy. CYP11B1 blockade raises 11-deoxycortisol and upstream precursors.

object.summary: Steroidogenesis inhibitors lower cortisol by blocking adrenal enzymes, but each target creates a distinct pattern of speed, precursor accumulation, interaction, and organ toxicity.
object.application: Select and titrate from severity, speed, liver and cardiac risk, pregnancy potential, interactions, access, and the need for biochemical monitoring rather than treating the class as interchangeable.

lesson.heading: Block CYP11B1
lesson.body: Osilodrostat and metyrapone inhibit 11-beta-hydroxylase, lowering cortisol while increasing upstream precursors. Monitor for hypocortisolism, hypokalemia, hypertension, edema, androgenic effects, and QT-related risk where applicable.

lesson.body: Isturisa now covers adult endogenous Cushing syndrome when surgery is unavailable or unsuccessful. Usual initiation is 2 mg twice daily; increases are spaced at least two weeks apart, with a 30 mg twice-daily ceiling. Hepatic impairment requires lower starting doses. Every approach requires education for hypocortisolism and stress illness.

Hypocortisolism can occur with every effective synthesis inhibitor.

object.summary: Supplement injury can present as liver failure, arrhythmia, hypertension, hypokalemia, seizure, or kidney injury. Product variability and multi-ingredient blends make causal assessment difficult but do not justify delayed care.
